claims.contract_text: The continuous-time PLRNN formulation (Equation 5, Section 3.1) solves the piecewise-linear ODE analytically within each of the 2^P linear subregions by tracking switching times between regions, bypassing numerical integration entirely (Section 3.1, Equation 5).
claims.boundary: One-dimensional source-inspired regional trajectory and switch only; no cPLRNN matrix solution, interval root finder, implicit-gradient training, or benchmark.

claims.contract_text: Equilibria and limit cycles of trained cPLRNNs are determined semi-analytically per region using a SCYFI-style fixed-point search and the trajectory-tracking equations 14-16 (Section 3.2).
claims.boundary: One-dimensional regional fixed-point enumeration only; no trained model, limit-cycle solve, or trajectory-tracking reproduction.

claims.contract_text: On irregularly-sampled leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) data, the standard discrete-time PLRNN fails badly with D_stsp=4.3±0.3, while the cPLRNN reconstructs the attractor accurately with D_stsp=0.26±0.03 (Table 3).
claims.boundary: Paper table and protocol are pinned; LIF data, trained models, traces, and metric outputs are absent.

claims.contract_text: cPLRNN trains roughly 4-5x faster than Neural ODE baselines using RK4 or Tsit5 solvers while matching their reconstruction performance (Table 2).
claims.boundary: Paper timing table is pinned; no local training, timing, or matched-quality logs are present.

claims.contract_text: On real neuronal recordings, cPLRNN attains D_stsp=0.71±0.02, slightly outperforming Neural ODE competitors on the same benchmark (Table 4).
